reconcile.note: Gill limits God's oath in Genesis 8:21 to never repeating a universal flood, leaving room for the more limited earthly judgments described by Isaiah and Malachi.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Will God curse the earth?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/curse_earth.html) (2013).

sides.snippet: I will not again curse the ground any more for man's sake
sides.verseText: Yahweh smelled the sweet savor. Yahweh said in his heart, \"I will not again curse the ground any more for man's sake, because the imagination of man's heart is evil from his youth; neither will I ever again strike everything living, as I have done.

sides.snippet: Therefore has the curse devoured the earth, and those who dwell therein are found guilty
sides.verseText: Therefore has the curse devoured the earth, and those who dwell therein are found guilty: therefore the inhabitants of the earth are burned, and few men left.
